bugClass.title: First-start date gate blocks previously started work
bugClass.cause: A due-date check intended to control the first unattended start also governs continuation. When the due date is still in the future, the shared gate can reject a replacement process restoring a checkpoint or prevent an already-started live session from reopening after an answer.
bugClass.criteria: Match either a checkpoint or reboot recovery path that cannot relaunch previously started work, or a post-answer path that cannot reopen its already-started live session. Trace the continuation through the request, queue, claim, host-start, or resume logic and identify the first-start date predicate that rejects or suppresses it. Verify ownership and a prior start for the same execution using a persisted start timestamp, a recorded start event, or a checkpoint linked to a started execution. A claim, retry count, answer, or resume label alone is insufficient. Untouched future-due work and retries that have never started still belong behind the first-start gate.

candidates.evidence: WatchdogRecoveryService.ts lines 74–94 check answer and status timing, require a matching item ID, tmux, a persisted startedAt, and no exit code, and exclude finished blocked runs superseded by a newer started run. outsideOwner distinguishes other-host, unassigned, and opted-out cases for targeted recovery. The excerpt ends before any reopen or relaunch decision involving the due date.

trackerAnswerDelivery.ts lines 90–108 call submitAnswer only when the run belongs to the local node and record a receipt on success. A finished run with keepBlocked exits before alerting, and other failures wait through a grace period. The excerpt omits submitAnswer's reopen logic, proof of prior start for that run, and any due-date predicate.

runClaim.ts lines 117–136 define a startup-expiry outcome and an unstartedRun check limited to queued runs with a null started_at, no session identifiers, and no active attempt. The excerpt ends at the claimHold signature, leaving the due-date predicate and its effect on recovery unverified.

trackerHostAdapter.ts lines 48–52 expose a hasStarted lookup that checks any persisted run for the item and a dueOwner callback that returns the designated runner. The excerpt leaves the continuation call path, the specific execution being resumed, and any date-based rejection unverified.

trackerHostRunEvents.ts lines 55–64 uses the receipt’s start and end timestamps and emits `answered-without-session` only for a resolved blocked item answered at or after that run started. The excerpt ends at event creation, leaving execution ownership and any downstream due-date gate unverified.

runResume.ts lines 76–90 pass the same blocked run's prior-start flag to automaticRequestHold and require a matching request, no open session, and no later started run on the same node. Lines 95–101 use that result for the answered blocked item. The hold predicate and downstream launch checks are absent, so a future due date blocking recovery is unverified.

runTransition.ts lines 52–74 record a session ID and start timestamp when a queued reservation with dispatch_at passes matchesSession, then call recoveryStarted. The excerpt ends at the recovery-source condition. It leaves the prior execution linkage, relaunch path, and any due-date predicate unverified.

TrackerRecurringService.ts lines 76–89 observe claimed work, start other work only after a successful claim, and enqueue a wake after receipt settlement only when settlement reports a pending wake, an outcome wake exists, and the signal is active. A claim alone does not establish prior start. The excerpt does not link the wake to the same started execution or show a downstream due-date predicate.
